Justice > Intelligence > Actors: native producers

This is a native source extraction. It records instruction operands, dispatch
arrays, field offsets and reconstructed append flow. It does not execute the
translation implementation or the game. The two PE image paths come from
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. All addresses below are RVAs in the reference
image unless a classic address is explicitly stated.

Entry and body ownership
------------------------
actor entry creation and plot title construction:
  reference 0x2b6760..0x2b9040; classic 0x2b4320..0x2b6c00.
actor title and body supplier:
  reference 0xd1840..0xd1eeb; classic 0xd17d0..0xd1e7b.
The fortress renderer invokes the body supplier for its selected actor and for
the displayed cards. The title is actor_entryst.p_list_name at +0x58. Body lines
are heap std::string pointers in actor.main_text_box's vector at +0x78..+0x80.

actor_entryst layout used by these native instructions:
  +0x00 historical_figure*
  +0x08 identity*
  +0x10 language_name*
  +0x18 list_name (full source title)
  +0x38 simple_list_name
  +0x58 p_list_name (native shortened title)
  +0x78 body vector begin; +0x80 end; +0x88 capacity
  +0xA0 alias identity id vector begin; +0xA8 end; +0xB0 capacity
  +0xB8 principle_org*
  +0xC0 associated_org* vector begin; +0xC8 end
  +0xD8 associated_plot* vector begin; +0xE0 end
  +0xF0 actor flags
organization_entryst +0x18 is its full list_name, +0x90 principle_actor_entry*.
An organization list_name is built from its principle actor name; it is not a
historical_entity name. Therefore Associated Organization often contains a
person's generated name, as in the user's screenshot.
plot_entryst +0x00 full list_name; +0x60 agreement*; +0x68 master_hfid;
  +0x70 organization_name.

Actor source title
------------------
Entry constructor's actor name selection at 0x2b68db..0x2b69af:
  if knowledge flags byte +0x04 has bit 0x08:
    if historical figure's language_name.has_name is set:
      name = language_name(figure +0x38, capitalize=true, extra=false)
      actor.name_ptr = figure +0x38
    else name = "Nameless"
  else if known alias_identity_id vector is nonempty:
    identity = lookup(first alias id)
    if identity and identity name getter returns a named language_name:
      name = language_name(identity name, capitalize=true, extra=false)
      actor.name_ptr = identity name
      actor.iden = identity
    else name = "Nameless"
  else name = "Unidentified"
The organization principle actor name repeats the same selection flow at
0x2b79e3..0x2b7a9d. Names can contain a first name, a nickname in `...' quotes,
compound language words, articles, and an "of" part. Nickname options are read
from the native name display settings. The full language_name and word-form
producers are retained as reference-language-name.asm/reference-language-word.asm
and their classic counterparts. Generated field values are world-dependent;
they are not a finite list of screenshot names.

Actor title shorten production
-------------------------------
reference 0x52d910..0x52ded4; classic 0x52b330..0x52b8f4.
The actor supplier calls this routine at reference 0xd18c8 / classic 0xd1858
only after copying full list_name into an empty p_list_name and finding its byte
length greater than max_bytes. The complete title remains in actor.list_name.

shorten(title, max_bytes):
  if title begins with case-insensitive ASCII "A ":
    delete the space and the A/a;
    if title.bytes <= max_bytes: return;
  if title begins with case-insensitive ASCII "An ":
    delete the space, N/n, then A/a;
    if title.bytes <= max_bytes: return;
  if title begins with case-insensitive ASCII "The ":
    delete the space, E/e, H/h, then T/t;
    if title.bytes <= max_bytes: return;
  // Each article is an independently tested leading-byte branch. The three
  // branches run in this order while the title remains above max_bytes.
  for index = title.bytes-1 down to 1:
    if title[index-1] == ASCII space: continue;
    if title[index] is one of a/e/i/o/u/A/E/I/O/U:
      erase exactly that byte;
      if title.bytes <= max_bytes: return;
  if title.bytes > max_bytes:
    title = its first max_bytes bytes;
  return;

The reverse vowel pass preserves byte zero and the first byte of every word
whose previous byte is ASCII space. It deletes no consonants and no additional
spaces. The final fallback writes the shortened byte length and a terminating
NUL at that length. No dot, ellipsis, replacement character or other text is
appended. A shortened actor title can therefore be neither a full-title prefix
nor a contiguous substring: it is the full title with bytes deleted in order.
The association body strings use raw prefix_bytes instead of this routine.

Both complete instruction bodies are retained as *-actor-title-shorten.asm.
Their call/jump edges and conditional branches are included in calls.tsv and
branches.tsv; functions.tsv identifies both ownership ranges and image paths.

Body supplier reconstructed append flow
--------------------------------------
max_bytes = 58;
if native graphic mode flag at VA 0x14189c298 is zero:
  max_bytes = native screen width at VA 0x1423cd784 - 4;
if actor.p_list_name.empty():
  actor.p_list_name = actor.list_name;
  shorten(actor.p_list_name, max_bytes);
if actor.body.begin != actor.body.end:
  return;  // body is lazy cached; its strings are not rebuilt each draw
for alias_id in actor.alias_identity_id:
  if actor.iden && actor.iden.id == alias_id: continue;
  identity = lookup(alias_id);
  if !identity || !identity.name.has_name: continue;
  body.push("Alias: " + language_name(identity.name, true, false));
if actor.principle_org:
  if actor.principle_org.principle_actor_entry == actor:
    body.push("Highest known in organization");
  else:
    body.push(prefix_bytes("Associated Organization: " +
                           actor.principle_org.list_name, max_bytes));
for org in actor.associated_org:
  if org == actor.principle_org: continue;
  body.push(prefix_bytes("Associated Organization: " + org.list_name,
                         max_bytes));
for plot in actor.associated_plot:
  body.push(prefix_bytes("Associated Plot: " + plot.list_name, max_bytes));

Alias rows do not use max_bytes truncation. The association rows truncate the
assembled English prefix AND dynamic value before rendering. The full source
names and plot title remain available in the referenced native records. The
renderer can therefore receive an incomplete prefix or incomplete generated
name even though the underlying data is complete.

Plot title source
-----------------
agreement +0x28/+0x30 is its vector<agreement_details*>.
agreement_details +0x04 agree_year; +0x10 data pointer; +0x18 subject enum.
The plot title starts as "A plot". An empty details vector leaves that fallback.
Only the first detail determines the displayed title. The title switch is the
11-entry array at 0x2b8f48 (classic 0x2b6b08), indexed by subject - 5. Values
outside 5..15, and value 12 (Location), retain "A plot" with no year suffix.

Every recognized normal subject below appends ", agreed in " + decimal(year),
including bare titles whose optional target ids are -1. Only subject 11 uses
the different " in " + decimal(year) suffix.

5 PositionCorruption (branch 0x2b6cd4):
  title = "Corrupt";
  if data.position_id@+0x14 != -1 && data.target_entity_id@+0x10 != -1:
    title += " ";
    entity = lookup(data.target_entity_id);
    assignment = entity ? lookup(entity.positions.own, position_id) : null;
    position = assignment ? entity_position_for_assignment(assignment) : null;
    if position:
      // dl=-1, r8b=0, r9b=0 chooses the generic singular title at position+0x98.
      title += capitalize(position.generic_singular) + " of";
    title += " " + entity_name(data.target_entity_id);
  // If any lookup in the position path fails, the entity is still appended.
6 PlotStealArtifact (0x2b6c82):
  title = "Steal";
  if data.artifact_id@+0x0C != -1:
    title += " " + artifact_name(data.artifact_id);
7 PromisePosition (0x2b6dde):
  title = "Provide Position";
  if data.entity_id@+0x28 != -1:
    title += " in " + entity_name(data.entity_id);
8 PlotAssassination (0x2b6c79):
  title = "Assassinate";
  if data.target_hfid@+0x0C != -1:
    title += " " + historical_figure_name(data.target_hfid);
9 PlotAbduct (0x2b6c01):
  title = "Abduct";
  if data.target_hfid@+0x0C != -1:
    title += " " + historical_figure_name(data.target_hfid);
10 PlotSabotage (0x2b6bbe):
  title = "Sabotage";
  if data.target_entity_id@+0x10 != -1:
    title += " " + entity_name(data.target_entity_id);
  else if data.target_hfid@+0x0C != -1:
    title += " " + historical_figure_name(data.target_hfid);
11 PlotConviction (0x2b6e25):
  // data +0x00..+0x18 is the criminal-index vector.
  switch data.corruption_action@+0x18:
    0 BRIBE_OFFICIAL: title = "Attempted Bribery";
    2 CORRUPT_IN_PLACE_GENERALLY: title = "Attempted Espionage";
    3 INDUCE_TO_EMBEZZLE: title = "Attempted Embezzlement";
    default: title remains "A plot";
  title += " in " + decimal(year);
  // No organization field is appended in this subject. No "agreed" suffix.
12 Location:
  title remains "A plot" and no suffix is added.
13 PlotInfiltrationCoup (0x2b6e8b):
  title = "Infiltrate";
  if data.target_entity_id@+0x08 != -1:
    title += " " + entity_name(data.target_entity_id);
14 PlotFrameTreason (0x2b6ed2):
  title = "Frame";
  if data.target_hfid@+0x08 != -1:
    title += " " + historical_figure_name(data.target_hfid);
15 PlotInduceWar (0x2b6f25):
  title = "Start War";
  if data.attacker_entity_id@+0x08 != -1 &&
     data.defender_entity_id@+0x0C != -1:
    title += " between " + entity_name(data.attacker_entity_id) +
             " and " + entity_name(data.defender_entity_id);

For Corrupt's failed position lookup, the native flow writes two separating
spaces before the entity: one at 0x2b6d02 and another at 0x2b6dae. This is a
real native append variant, not a new semantic target kind. The full normal
suffix is at 0x2b6f9d and year append at 0x2b6fb9.

Called target fields and finite fallback literals
------------------------------------------------
The normal plot constructor initializes a description context with identities
null, all ids -1 and flags 0 before historical_figure_name. It passes generic
gender/capitalization words set to 1. Thus the helper's interrogation labels
"interrogator"/"subject" and identity-specific "an unidentified creature" are
retained in the helper source but are not selected by this normal plot path.
reference 0xb92f10..0xb93927 / classic 0xb8ff50..0xb90967:
  absent historical_figure id -> "an unknown creature";
  available named figure -> generated language_name;
  unnamed figure -> caste/creature raw name with "a "/"the ", optionally
    "zombie " or "ghostly " as selected by the native creature state.
reference 0xb92900..0xb92a78 / classic 0xb8f940..0xb8fab8:
  absent historical_entity id -> "an unknown civilization";
  available entity -> generated language_name of the entity.
reference 0xb94400..0xb94710 / classic 0xb91440..0xb91750:
  absent artifact id -> "an unknown artifact";
  artifact title missing -> "Untitled";
  artifact existing -> generated artifact language_name or stored book title.
LPAGE markers retained in the helpers are emitted only when their context flag
requests a Legends hyperlink; normal actor plot construction passes false.

Additional same-constructor graph fields
---------------------------------------
The latter half of actor-entries constructs the Organizations/Plots hierarchy.
Those fields share the producer but are separate from Actors card body strings.
Its fixed graph labels are "Boss", "Membr", "Thief", "Crrpt", "Assas", "Snatc",
"Sabtr", "Framr", "Asset", and deceased status "RIP". Switch arrays at
0x2b8f74, 0x2b8fa0 and 0x2b8fcc describe party/role selection and label selection;
their exact targets for all 5..15 subject values are retained in switches.tsv.
These graph labels must not be mistaken for omitted Actors card prose.

Data files
----------
functions.tsv records native function ownership and image identities.
literals.tsv records printable RIP-relative operands and short inline fragments.
calls.tsv records direct call and jump targets, with instruction kind preserved.
branches.tsv records every conditional jump in the selected native functions.
switches.tsv records every relevant subject and language-word dispatch slot.
*-actor-associations.asm and *-actor-entries.asm retain every instruction in both
native functions, including the lazy-cache and optional/missing-id branches.
The remaining .asm files retain the dynamic field name, position, word and year
producers called by these title constructors. This inventory describes finite
branches and dynamic field construction; a game's generated values have no
finite exhaustive catalogue of literal complete sentences.
